column5: Gap real (no CS inheritance topic; only compiler type-system polymorphism). Wrong: "super(...) must be the first statement" in Java is outdated; JEP 513 (JDK 25, final) allows prologue statements that do not reference the object (openjdk.org JEP 513, jdk-dev mail 2025-05). Edited to say "before Java 25". Python AttributeError example, private-field rule, constructors-not-inherited, Object/object roots verified. Prereqs exist, all formal-systems.

Gap real (dynamic dispatch only mentioned in compilers bytecode/escape-analysis topics). Q1 Woof, Q2 compile error and cast, overloading vs overriding (compile-time vs run-time selection), @Override check, super.m()/super().m() verified against Java/Python semantics.

Gap real (no "abstract class" anywhere in domains/). Java abstract instantiation compile error, concrete subclass must implement abstract methods, single extends/multiple implements, Comparable<T>.compareTo, Java 8 default methods, Python abc @abstractmethod TypeError on instantiation verified.

Gap real (no 2D-array topic). Worked: new int[3][5] gives length 3 and 5; [[0]*3]*2 then grid[0][0]=7 prints [[7, 0, 0], [7, 0, 0]] (shared row); column-sum loop correct; ragged arrays in Java correct.

Gap real (only crypto PRNG and advanced Monte Carlo topics exist; none at CS1/AP CSP level). Worked: (int)(Math.random()*6)+1 gives 1..6; *7 gives 0..6; (int)Math.random()*6+1 always 1. P(two dice sum 7)=6/36=1/6 about 0.167; quarter-circle fraction pi/4. randint inclusive, random() half-open, seeding determinism checked against Python docs semantics.
Gap real (only asynchronous-io-and-aio at OS level). tkinter command=save_file() passes None, addEventListener form, mainloop, single-threaded blocking all correct.

Gap real (no version-control topic in domains/). Git by Linus Torvalds 2005 for Linux kernel correct; commit without add makes no commit ("no changes added to commit"); git commit -a, git switch -c, content hash IDs, conflict rule all correct.

Gap real (digital-citizenship-responsibility only mentions copyright in passing; no licensing topic). Automatic copyright (Berne), idea/expression distinction, GPL copyleft vs MIT/BSD/Apache permissive, Linux kernel GPL, CC BY/SA/NC/ND, CC FAQ recommends against CC licenses for software (creativecommons.org/faq) all correct.

Gap real (no search-in-array topic below binary-search-algorithm). Worked: buggy else-return checks only index 0; worst case 1,000 comparisons; binary search worst about 10 probes for 1,000 (ceil log2 1001 = 10) and about 20 for 10^6; average (n+1)/2; first occurrence index 3.

Gap real (only NFV/network virtualization and bytecode VMs). Popek and Goldberg 1974 CACM condition (sensitive subset of privileged), x86 non-trapping sensitive instructions (e.g. POPF), VMware binary translation, Xen paravirtualization, VT-x 2005/AMD-V 2006, EPT, Type 1/Type 2 examples, namespaces/cgroups all correct.

Gap real (no journaling/fsck content anywhere in CS). Crash-point analysis matches OSTEP Ch. 42; commit-block rule, checkpointing, double write, ext4 default data=ordered, ext3/NTFS journaling, ZFS/Btrfs copy-on-write all correct.

Gap real (no RAID topic). Worked: P = 1011^0110^1100 = 0001; rebuild D1 = 1011^1100^0001 = 0110; RAID 5 5x4 TB = 16 TB usable; small write = 4 I/Os. Patterson, Gibson and Katz 1988 SIGMOD paper; RAID 4 parity bottleneck, RAID 6 N-2 correct.

Gap real (multicore only mentioned in passing in power-thermal and thread topics). Worked: Amdahl 1/(0.10+0.90/8)=1/0.2125=4.71, limit 10x. Dynamic power ~ C V^2 f, mid-2000s power wall, Flynn 1966 MIMD, coarse/fine/simultaneous MT, Hyper-Threading as SMT correct.

Gap real (no GPU topic). NVIDIA warp = 32 threads, SIMT term, streaming multiprocessors, divergence masking, latency hiding by warp switching, coalescing, CUDA/OpenCL, lower GPU clocks, PCIe copy overhead correct. Per-thread PC hedged "in the programming model" (true since Volta).

Gap real (join methods only mentioned in query-optimization, cardinality and EXPLAIN topics). Worked (Silberschatz 7e Ch. 15 formulas): block NLJ b_r*b_s+b_r = 100*1000+100 = 100,100; reversed 101,000; tuple NLJ n_r*b_s+b_r; merge b_r+b_s; hash join ~3(b_r+b_s). Equi-join restriction and recursive partitioning correct.

Gap real (no TRC/DRC topic). Codd's theorem (Codd 1972, "Relational Completeness of Data Base Sublanguages"), safety definition, TRC ID-projection form matches Silberschatz, QBE (Zloof, IBM, 1970s) based on DRC, division for "for all" queries correct.

Gap real (CSMA/CA in wireless-networking-802-11 and CSMA/CD in ethernet-protocol, but no ALOHA/partitioning/taking-turns survey). Worked: slotted ALOHA 1/e = 0.37, pure 1/(2e) = 0.18; BEB n=3 gives K in {0..7}, cap n=10, 512 bit times (Kurose and Ross 6.3); TDMA 1/10 share. ALOHAnet, University of Hawaii, Abramson, about 1970 correct.

Gap real (linker only mentioned in passing in OS memory topics). Symbol resolution/relocation, sections starting at 0 in .o files, -lm for libm, static .a member selection, PIC, execve/dynamic linker/_start, multiple-definition error match CS:APP Ch. 7.

Gap real (no PEAS/rational-agent topic in CS). Rationality definition, PEAS, environment dimensions, agent types, vacuum performance-measure example, taxi and poker classifications match Russell and Norvig Ch. 2 (taxi: partial, multi, stochastic, sequential, dynamic, continuous; poker: partial, multi, stochastic, sequential). Simple reflex sufficient only if fully observable matches R&N.

Gap real (UCS/IDS appear only in passing in alpha-beta and external-memory topics). Worked: IDS b=10,d=5: 50+400+3000+20000+100000 = 123,450; BFS 10+100+1000+10000+100000 = 111,110 (matches R&N); IDS space O(bd), DFS O(bm), BFS O(b^d), bidirectional O(b^(d/2)); BFS frontier at d=8 ~10^8.

Gap real (STRIPS/PDDL absent elsewhere except one passing mention in sat-canonical-problem). Fikes and Nilsson 1971 STRIPS at SRI for Shakey; PDDL 1998 for the IPC (McDermott); FF, Graphplan, SATPlan; Move(b,x,y) schema matches R&N; delete-relaxation h+ NP-hard; worked Go action state = {At(Robot,Lab), Holding(Box)}; Sussman anomaly analysis and plan (C to table, B on C, A on B) correct.

Gap real (RPC only a word in observability topics). Wrong: "with at-most-once semantics, the server tags each request with a unique ID"; the client assigns the request ID and the server filters duplicates (Birrell and Nelson 1984 call IDs; van Steen and Tanenbaum). Edited. Birrell and Nelson, Xerox PARC, 1984 TOCS; stubs, marshalling, byte order, gRPC/Protocol Buffers, Thrift, copy-restore, timeout ambiguity all correct.

Gap real (no MapReduce/Hadoop mentions elsewhere). Checked against Dean and Ghemawat OSDI 2004: 16-64 MB splits, hash(key) mod R, master pings workers, completed map tasks re-run on failure (local disk) but completed reduce tasks not (GFS), backup tasks for stragglers, combiner valid for commutative and associative reduce. Spark in-memory iteration point correct.

Gap real (CPA/CCA mentioned in modes, PRF, RSA topics but no definitions topic). Wrong: "any deterministic scheme fails CPA security in two oracle queries"; one query (Enc(m0)) suffices, as the file's own Q1 says (Katz and Lindell). Edited to "a single oracle query". Goldwasser and Micali early 1980s semantic security/indistinguishability equivalence, Vaudenay 2002 padding oracle, CTR malleability CCA attack, encrypt-then-MAC with strongly secure MAC gives CCA, negligible-function definition, Shannon key-length bound correct.

Gap real (no computational-geometry topic). Worked: orientation (4)(3)-(0)(2) = 12 > 0, left turn. Wrong 1: Q2 option "a million random points inside a triangle, where the hull has only a handful of vertices"; Renyi and Sulanke 1963 give E[h] ~ (2k/3) ln n = 2 ln 10^6 ~ 28 for a triangle, above log2 n ~ 20, so gift wrapping is not clearly faster; replaced with a 3-vertex hull and h = 3 in the explanation. Wrong 2: popped point "lies inside the triangle formed by its neighbors and p" names only two points; corrected to triangle p0, entry below, p (CLRS 33.3), in Q4 and Explainer. Graham 1972, Jarvis 1973, Chan 1996 O(n log h), parabola reduction to sorting, O(nh) correct.
